claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. I'll need to ask you a few questions to assess your situation.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 16 and lives at home with me. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can see you have a son named Alex who is 16 and lives at home with you.

Since Alex is 16, there are some additional considerations. Let me ask you:

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he in school, college, sixth form, or an approved training program?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment. He left school and hasn't started anything else yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 16 and not currently in education or training, I need to ask:

**Has Alex registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services?** 

(If he has, you may still be able to get Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks after leaving education.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with any careers service or the armed forces. He's just been at home since leaving school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. I have a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is Alex working at all? And if so, how many hours per week does he work?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at the moment. He's just been taking some time to figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Just a couple more questions:

**Is Alex claiming any benefits in his own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not claiming any benefits himself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One final question to complete my assessment:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

While you normally qualify for Child Benefit for children under 16, the rules change once a child reaches 16 years old. For children aged 16 or over (up to age 20), Child Benefit can continue **only if** they stay in approved education or training.

Since Alex:
- Is 16 and has left school
- Is not currently in any approved education or training
- Has not registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services

He does not meet the eligibility criteria for continued Child Benefit.

**What could change this:**
- If Alex enrolls in approved education or training (such as college, sixth form, or an approved training program), you could claim Child Benefit again
- If he registers with a careers service, you may be able to claim for up to 20 weeks

If Alex's circumstances change and he does start education, training, or registers with a careers service, you should contact the Child Benefit Office to update them and potentially restart your claim.

For children aged 16 or over, you'll still qualify if your child is under 20 AND they stay in approved education or training. Alex is not currently in approved education or training. Additionally, Alex has not registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services (which would allow Child Benefit to continue for 20 weeks after leaving education or training). Since Alex is 16, not in approved education or training, and has not registered with a careers service or armed services, he does not meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit. The rules specifically state that Child Benefit stops when a child aged 16 or 17 is no longer in approved education or training, unless they have registered with a careers service (which provides a 20-week extension). As Alex has done neither, you are not eligible for Child Benefit for him.
